summary: Racing AI that slows into corners, rubber-bands and recovers when stuck, all through an internal state machine.
overview: Assign an ordered waypoint path and it drives: easing off into corners, catching up or backing off relative to a rubber-band target, and reversing out when stuck. The behaviour switching is a StateMachine wired internally, so no custom IState code is needed to use it.
useCases: AI opponents on a lap-based track.
Keeping a race close with rubber-banding.
A demo or attract-mode car that drives itself.

params.tuning: Zero ignores corners entirely and the AI understeers into walls. This is the main difference between a car that looks driven and one that looks scripted.
Usually the player. Unassigned, rubber-banding is off and the AI races at its own pace.
Keep it modest. Large values are visible to the player as cheating.
Too short and normal slow corners trigger a recovery reverse mid-race.

gotchas.title: It follows waypoints, it does not know the track
gotchas.body: There is no collision or racing line awareness. A path that cuts a corner too tightly drives into the barrier every lap.

gotchas.title: Rubber-banding is noticeable if overdone
gotchas.body: A large boost keeps races close and makes the player's skill feel irrelevant. Small values, or only applying it when far behind, reads better.
